recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR core follow-up is needed for FHIR-6905 unless a future work group decision changes the broader Questionnaire answerValueSet/answerOption design.
issue_request: FHIR-6905 was a Published FHIR-core Questionnaire change request, resolved Not Persuasive with Modification, asking why DSTU1 Questionnaire question options referenced a ValueSet rather than embedding local answer choices. The accepted action was to retain ValueSet as the reusable answer-set mechanism and add guidance for using ValueSet as a contained resource.
initial_application: The issue was applied in SVN #5941, imported as git commit 26e8b597d5034f4372a848e5660a88268f4b664c, which explicitly listed {#6905} and added Questionnaire notes explaining ValueSet-backed choices and contained ValueSets.
additional_context: Questionnaire is active in source/fhir.ini. Later Questionnaire changes renamed and remodeled the old options/choices surface, and the current narrative now explains answerOption versus answerValueSet while preserving the contained ValueSet guidance. Current examples include Questionnaire-contained ValueSets referenced by fragment identifiers.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit on the combined branch. No source hunk was necessary because source/questionnaire/questionnaire-notes.xml already contains the requested contained ValueSet guidance and source/questionnaire/questionnaire-example-gcs.xml demonstrates it.
